candidates.requirement: Make successful uncompress of supported zlib streams producing more than 65,025 bytes reachable.
candidates.target_route: The entry derives output capacity from data[0] times data[1], then calls uncompress once with the entire input.
candidates.failure_condition: A valid zlib stream containing two 32,768-byte stored blocks of zeroes produces 65,536 bytes. The harness allocates at most 255 × 255 = 65,025 bytes, so this supported call cannot complete successfully.
candidates.alternative_paths: The complete entry makes no second call or capacity adjustment; every input has the same 65,025-byte maximum.

before.requirement: Reach successful uncompress of a valid zlib stream producing 65,536 bytes.
before.reason: The old decoder accepts successive stored blocks, but the one-shot wrapper uses the target's smaller output capacity and cannot reach stream end.

after.requirement: Reach successful uncompress of a valid zlib stream producing 65,536 bytes.
after.reason: The new tree-clearing call is on the Huffman path; stored-block decoding and the one-shot capacity requirement remain the same.

claims.reason: The same input-derived buffer limit blocks the same supported 65,536-byte output before and after. The changed tree-clearing operation does not affect this stored-block witness.
